{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The corporate tax rate is cut from 35% to 20% in both bills.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The average effective tax rate on US corporations is about 15%.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"In 1962 corporate taxes represented 25% of federal revenue.",

"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Both bills would penalize states that use taxation to fund public goods by cutting or eliminating the tax deduction for state and local taxes (SALT).",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The top six states targeted by the cut in the SALT deduction are CA, CT, MD, NJ, NY, and OR.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"CA, CT, MD, NJ, NY, and OR all voted for Clinton.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"CA, CT, MD, NJ, NY, and OR all have minimum wages well above the federal level.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"CA, CT, MD, NJ, NY, and OR are more unionized than the US as a whole.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Trump/GOP tax proposals punish liberal states.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
